title: Check your T-fal kettle: a 4.18-million-unit recall is still causing fire alerts
summary: Japan's Consumer Affairs Agency again flagged recalled T-fal electric kettles in its September 11 serious-accident bulletin. The recall covers specific lots among 4,185,393 kettles, and the remedy is a free replacement of the power base.
why_it_matters: This recall began in 2025 but remains an active safety issue. Owners can identify affected units from the product number and four-digit manufacturing code on the kettle base instead of guessing from brand or appearance.

sources.title: Serious product accidents: recalled electric kettle, rechargeable speaker, electric-assist bicycle and rechargeable pressure washer (September 11)

sources.publisher: Consumer Affairs Agency Recall Information Site
sources.title: Groupe SEB Japan: T-fal electric kettles — free power-base replacement
Important: free replacement of electric-kettle power bases

claims.text: The Consumer Affairs Agency's September 11, 2026 serious-product-accident bulletin again highlighted a recalled electric kettle sold by Groupe SEB Japan, with free power-base replacement as the remedy.
The recall covers specific manufacturing lots among 4,185,393 T-fal electric kettles.
claims.basis: Consumer Affairs Agency recall database and manufacturer notice.

claims.text: The affected lots were manufactured between October 2021 and July 2024, and owners identify them using both the product number and four-digit code on the kettle base.
The recall was initiated because plug damage under certain cord-use conditions can lead to smoke or ignition near the outlet.

content.who_is_affected: Anyone in Japan who owns a T-fal electric kettle manufactured in the relevant 2021-2024 period should check the exact product number and four-digit manufacturing code. Not every T-fal kettle is affected.
content.when: The recall remains active; the Consumer Affairs Agency highlighted it again on September 11, 2026.
content.financial_impact: The official remedy for affected units is a free replacement of the power base.
content.risk_if_ignored: HIGH — affected power bases can be associated with smoke or ignition near the electrical outlet.
content.potential_benefit: Remove a known household fire risk without paying for the replacement remedy.
content.downside: Checking the label takes a few minutes; owners must match both identifiers rather than relying on model appearance alone.
content.what_would_change_mind: A manufacturer or regulator notice ending, narrowing or changing the recall remedy.

action_plan.goal: Determine whether your T-fal kettle is affected and request the official free power-base replacement if it is.
action_plan.who_should_act: Owners of T-fal electric kettles, especially units manufactured from October 2021 through July 2024. Owners of other brands can ignore this specific recall.
action_plan.deadline: No end date is stated in the cited recall notice; check now because the recall remains active.
prepare: Access to the label or marking on the bottom of the kettle
Internet access to the official T-fal or Consumer Affairs Agency recall page

steps.action: Turn the kettle off, unplug it and inspect the bottom label or marking for the product number and four-digit code.
steps.how: Use the official recall page's identification guide; some models have the information engraved instead of on a label.
steps.done_when: You have recorded both the product number and four-digit code.

steps.action: Compare both identifiers with the affected combinations on the official T-fal recall page.
steps.how: Do not decide based only on the brand name, color or general model family.
steps.done_when: You know whether your exact unit is listed as affected.

steps.action: Use the manufacturer recall channel linked from the official notice to request the free replacement power base.
steps.how: Follow the current manufacturer instructions rather than buying a third-party base.
steps.done_when: The official replacement request is accepted or you have direct manufacturer guidance.

mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming every T-fal kettle is recalled.
Continuing to use an affected unit because it has not yet shown visible damage.
Buying an unofficial replacement base before checking the free recall remedy.

decision_rules.if: Both identifiers match the official affected list
decision_rules.then: Use the official recall process for the free power-base replacement.
This specific recall does not apply, but continue normal safe-use guidance.

action_plan.follow_up: Re-check the manufacturer recall page if the identification table or remedy is updated.

outcomes: Recognize why an older recall can still be a current safety story.
Know how to identify an affected kettle without guessing.
learning.background: A product recall stays relevant as long as affected products remain in homes. This T-fal action began in September 2025, but Japan's regulator again highlighted the product in a September 2026 serious-accident bulletin.

terms.meaning: The separate base that supplies electricity to a cordless kettle.
terms.why_it_matters: The recall remedy replaces this component rather than necessarily replacing the entire kettle.

how_it_works.title: Identify the exact production lot
how_it_works.explanation: The product number identifies the model, while the four-digit code narrows the manufacturing lot. Both are needed because only specific combinations are affected.

how_it_works.title: Remove the risk through the official remedy
how_it_works.explanation: For affected units, the manufacturer replaces the power base with a design using a different power plug structure.

learning.example: Two visually identical kettles can have different four-digit manufacturing codes, so one may be recalled while the other is not.
takeaways: 4,185,393 units are within the recall population, but only listed product/code combinations are affected.
Check the bottom markings, not just the model name.
The official remedy is a free power-base replacement.

30_sec: Japan's regulator flagged the T-fal kettle recall again on September 11.
Specific lots among 4.18 million kettles are covered.
Check the product number and four-digit code underneath the kettle.
Affected owners can request a free replacement power base.
reading_levels.2_min: The recall began in 2025 but remains active. Groupe SEB Japan says specific manufacturing lots of T-fal electric kettles made from October 2021 through July 2024 can suffer plug damage that may lead to smoke or ignition near an outlet. Owners should unplug the kettle, read the product number and four-digit manufacturing code underneath it, compare both with the official list, and use the manufacturer recall route if the unit matches.

editorial_visual.scene: a household electric kettle sitting unplugged beside a clearly separated power base while a protective shield symbol blocks a small stylized electrical spark near the wall outlet
editorial_visual.caption: An old recall can remain a current fire risk

title: Foreign residents: a real immigration survey is arriving by mail, while fake versions are circulating
summary: Japan's Immigration Services Agency is running its 2026 foreign-resident survey from September 11 to October 4 by mailing selected residents a paper invitation for an online response. The agency says it does not contact respondents by email or phone, never asks for bank or card details, and has already confirmed impersonation attempts.
why_it_matters: A legitimate government-looking envelope and a fake message may appear at the same time. Knowing the official contact pattern helps foreign residents avoid both unnecessary fear of the real survey and phishing through fake links.

claims.text: The 2026 Basic Survey on Foreign Residents runs from September 11 through October 4, 2026.
Selected respondents are sent a paper letter and then answer the survey online; participation is voluntary and responses do not affect immigration or residence procedures.
The Immigration Services Agency says impersonation attempts using suspicious email or phone contact have been confirmed.
claims.basis: Official scam warning on the survey page.

claims.text: The agency says it will not email or phone respondents, will not request bank-account or credit-card information, and does not ask people to answer through links sent by email.

content.who_is_affected: Foreign residents in Japan, especially people who receive a paper invitation to the 2026 Basic Survey on Foreign Residents or a message claiming to be about that survey.
content.when: Official survey period: September 11 through October 4, 2026.
content.financial_impact: The legitimate survey does not require bank or card information. A request for such information is a strong warning sign.
content.risk_if_ignored: HIGH if a fake email/phone request is trusted; LOW if the legitimate voluntary survey is simply not answered because participation itself is optional.
content.deadline: 2026-10-04 for the legitimate survey response period.
content.potential_benefit: Avoid phishing while recognizing the real government survey process.
content.downside: A cautious resident may mistake a legitimate mailed invitation for a scam unless they verify it against the official agency page.
content.what_would_change_mind: A later Immigration Services Agency notice changing the official survey channel or dates.

action_plan.goal: Verify survey contact safely and avoid fake email or phone requests.
action_plan.who_should_act: Foreign residents who receive a mailed survey invitation, email, phone call or message claiming to be connected to the 2026 Basic Survey on Foreign Residents.
prepare: The physical letter if one arrived
The official Immigration Services Agency survey webpage opened independently in your browser

steps.action: Separate a mailed paper invitation from email, phone or message contact.
steps.how: The official process uses a mailed letter for selected respondents; the agency says it does not email or phone respondents about this survey.
steps.done_when: You know whether the contact method matches the agency's stated process.

steps.action: Reject any request for bank-account or credit-card information or any email asking you to answer through a link.
steps.how: Compare the request with the warning on the official Immigration Services Agency page.
steps.done_when: No sensitive financial request or email-answer link remains unverified.

steps.action: Use the contact information published on the official agency page rather than contact details inside a suspicious message.
steps.how: Open the official page independently and use its listed survey inquiry route.
steps.done_when: You have confirmed whether the communication is genuine.

mistakes_to_avoid: Clicking an emailed survey link just because it uses government branding.
Giving bank or credit-card details to someone claiming they are required for the survey.
Assuming non-response will hurt visa or residence procedures; the agency says participation is voluntary and does not affect those procedures.

decision_rules.if: You received only an email or phone call claiming to be the survey
decision_rules.then: Treat it as suspicious and verify independently through the official agency page.

decision_rules.if: You received the official paper invitation and want to participate
decision_rules.then: Follow the instructions in the mailed material after verifying the survey page independently.

action_plan.follow_up: If the agency publishes a later warning or channel change, follow the newest official notice.

outcomes: Distinguish the real survey workflow from a phishing attempt.
Understand that participation is voluntary and separate from residence-status decisions.
learning.background: The Immigration Services Agency surveys foreign residents to understand work, daily-life and social issues that can inform coexistence policy. In 2026 it is simultaneously warning that scammers are impersonating this survey.

terms.meaning: A government survey of foreign residents' living and working conditions in Japan.
terms.why_it_matters: It is a policy-information survey, not a visa examination.

how_it_works.title: Legitimate contact starts with physical mail
how_it_works.explanation: Selected residents receive a paper envelope, then use the survey's online response method.

how_it_works.title: Scam attempts break that pattern
how_it_works.explanation: The agency specifically says it does not initiate this survey by email or phone and does not request banking or card information.

learning.example: An email saying 'answer the immigration survey here' with a clickable link does not match the agency's stated process, even if the message uses official-looking logos.
takeaways: The real invitation is sent by mail.
The agency says it will not email or phone respondents.
Bank/card information is not part of the legitimate survey.
Participation does not affect immigration procedures.

30_sec: The 2026 foreign-resident survey is real and runs September 11-October 4.
Selected residents are contacted by physical mail.
Immigration says it will not email or call about the survey and will not ask for bank/card details.
An emailed survey-answer link should be treated as suspicious.
reading_levels.2_min: Japan's Immigration Services Agency is conducting the 2026 Basic Survey on Foreign Residents. Selected residents receive a paper invitation and may answer online. Participation is voluntary and does not affect immigration procedures. The same official page warns that fake email and phone approaches have been confirmed. The agency says it will not email or phone respondents, request bank or credit-card data, or ask people to answer through an email link.

editorial_visual.scene: a sealed official-looking paper envelope on one side and a suspicious glowing email link on the other, separated by a strong protective shield symbol
editorial_visual.caption: The real survey starts with mail, not a phishing link

title: Tsukuba will subsidize children's flu vaccination from October 1
summary: Tsukuba residents from age 6 months through junior-high grade 3 can receive up to ¥2,000 toward one influenza vaccination between October 1, 2026 and January 31, 2027. The city says FluMist is eligible, and participating clinics apply the subsidy without a separate city application.
why_it_matters: Ibaraki's latest surveillance says influenza is already circulating and broader acute respiratory infections rose again in Week 36. Families can plan the appointment before the subsidy window opens instead of discovering the program after clinics become busy.

sources.title: Subsidy for pediatric influenza vaccination costs

claims.text: Tsukuba's 2026 pediatric influenza subsidy covers residents who are at least 6 months old through the equivalent of junior-high grade 3 on the vaccination date.
The subsidy period is October 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027, with a maximum subsidy of ¥2,000 for one vaccination during the period.
FluMist is eligible, and no separate city application is required when vaccination is received at a participating medical institution.
Ibaraki reported Week 36 acute respiratory infection surveillance at 55.46 reports per sentinel, up from 50.55 the prior week, and said influenza was currently circulating in the prefecture.

content.who_is_affected: Children registered as Tsukuba residents who are at least 6 months old through junior-high grade 3 equivalent on the vaccination date.
content.financial_impact: Up to ¥2,000 for one influenza vaccination during the subsidy period. The city states a higher maximum for public-assistance recipients.
content.risk_if_ignored: MED — the main consequence is missing a municipal subsidy and potentially delaying seasonal planning; vaccination decisions themselves should be made with the child's clinician when appropriate.
content.deadline: Vaccination must occur within the October 1, 2026-January 31, 2027 subsidy period.
content.potential_benefit: Reduce eligible out-of-pocket vaccination cost and arrange protection while respiratory infections are already active locally.
content.downside: The subsidy covers only one vaccination in the period; even when a child receives a two-dose schedule, only the first dose is subsidized under this program.
content.what_would_change_mind: A later Tsukuba City notice changing age eligibility, subsidy amount, eligible vaccine types, participating clinics or dates.

action_plan.goal: Use the Tsukuba subsidy correctly if your child is eligible and you choose influenza vaccination.
action_plan.who_should_act: Parents/guardians of Tsukuba-registered children aged 6 months through junior-high grade 3 equivalent. Families outside Tsukuba should check their own municipality instead.
action_plan.deadline: Vaccination must be given from October 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027.
prepare: Child's age and Tsukuba resident-registration status
A participating-clinic choice from the city list
Any clinic-specific items requested when booking

steps.action: Check that the child is registered in Tsukuba and falls within the city's age range on the vaccination date.
steps.how: Use the eligibility section of the official Tsukuba page.
steps.done_when: You have confirmed the child falls within the listed group.

steps.action: Open the city's participating-medical-institution list and contact a clinic for an appointment.
steps.how: The city says no separate municipal application is needed when using a participating clinic.
steps.done_when: An appointment or clinic plan is confirmed.

steps.step: Confirm vaccine and price with the clinic
steps.action: Ask the clinic which influenza vaccine it offers, the total price and the amount due after the city subsidy.
steps.how: FluMist is eligible under the city program, but vaccine suitability and availability are clinical/provider matters.
steps.done_when: You understand the scheduled vaccine and expected out-of-pocket cost.

mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming both doses are subsidized when a two-dose schedule is used; the city states the subsidy is for one vaccination.
Assuming any clinic automatically applies the subsidy; check the participating-institution list or the city's instructions for non-participating clinics.
Treating local surveillance as personal medical advice; it is a population signal.

decision_rules.if: Your child is eligible and you choose vaccination
decision_rules.then: Book within the subsidy period and use a participating clinic for the simplest process.

decision_rules.if: The child has a medical condition, prior vaccine reaction or you are unsure which vaccine is appropriate
decision_rules.then: Discuss the choice with the child's clinician rather than relying on the subsidy notice alone.

action_plan.follow_up: Check the city page again close to the appointment in case the participating-clinic list or operational details change.

outcomes: Understand exactly who qualifies and how much Tsukuba contributes.
Separate the municipal subsidy rules from the medical decision about vaccination.
learning.background: Municipalities in Japan can run their own vaccination-support programs. Tsukuba's 2026-27 program is a local subsidy, not a nationwide automatic payment. Separately, Ibaraki's infectious-disease surveillance indicates influenza is already circulating as the subsidy window approaches.

terms.meaning: A nasal-spray live attenuated influenza vaccine.
terms.why_it_matters: Tsukuba explicitly includes it as an eligible vaccine under this subsidy program.

terms.meaning: A system where designated medical institutions report cases so authorities can track community trends.
terms.why_it_matters: It describes population-level activity, not an individual child's probability of infection.

how_it_works.title: Municipal subsidy
how_it_works.explanation: At participating clinics, the city contribution is handled through the clinic rather than requiring a separate city application.

how_it_works.title: Local disease signal
how_it_works.explanation: The prefecture's surveillance helps families understand timing, but does not replace individual medical advice.

learning.example: If a participating clinic charges more than ¥2,000, an eligible family generally pays the remaining amount after the city's contribution; the exact clinic price should be confirmed directly.
takeaways: Eligible ages run from 6 months through junior-high grade 3 equivalent.
Maximum standard subsidy is ¥2,000 for one vaccination.
Use the city clinic list and confirm medical suitability with the provider.

30_sec: Tsukuba's child flu-vaccine subsidy starts October 1.
Eligible residents: age 6 months through junior-high grade 3 equivalent.
Standard support is up to ¥2,000 for one vaccination; FluMist qualifies.
Ibaraki says influenza is already circulating, so families can plan appointments now.
reading_levels.2_min: Tsukuba's program runs October 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027. Eligible children are registered Tsukuba residents aged at least 6 months through junior-high grade 3 equivalent. The standard subsidy is up to ¥2,000 for one vaccination; FluMist is included, and participating clinics do not require a separate city application. Ibaraki's Week 36 surveillance says influenza is already circulating and acute respiratory infection reports rose from 50.55 to 55.46 per sentinel, making early planning useful without turning a population signal into individual medical advice.

editorial_visual.scene: a parent and child calmly planning an autumn clinic visit beside a calendar opening on October 1, with a small protective shield and no needles shown
editorial_visual.caption: Plan the appointment before the subsidy window opens

title: Japan expands online-marketplace safety controls after asbestos products were found for sale
summary: Japan added asbestos-containing products and certain regulated protective/industrial equipment to its Product Safety Pledge on September 10. Officials say products found above the legal asbestos threshold have included colored craft sand and diatomaceous-earth bath mats, but that does not mean every product in those categories is contaminated.
why_it_matters: The change strengthens the framework used with major online marketplaces to identify and remove unsafe listings. For consumers, the useful lesson is to check official product notices rather than treating a whole product category as dangerous.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
sources.title: Information on distributed products containing asbestos

claims.text: On September 10, 2026, Japan expanded the Product Safety Pledge to cover asbestos-containing products regulated under the Industrial Safety and Health Act and certain regulated machines/equipment sold online.
Japanese law prohibits manufacture, import, transfer, provision and use of products containing more than 0.1% asbestos by weight, except limited cases such as research use.
claims.basis: Consumer Affairs Agency and Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare explanation of the legal threshold.

claims.text: Officials cited past findings involving colored sand and diatomaceous-earth bath mats as reasons for adding these products to the pledge framework.
claims.basis: Consumer Affairs Agency press conference and MHLW product-information history.

claims.text: The policy expansion should improve marketplace detection and removal of unsafe listings, but it does not establish that all colored sand or diatomaceous products are unsafe.
claims.basis: Scope of the Product Safety Pledge and the government's examples.

content.who_is_affected: People buying craft materials, diatomaceous products or regulated safety/industrial equipment through online marketplaces, and people who already own a specifically identified asbestos-containing product.
content.when: The additional product categories were announced as part of the Product Safety Pledge on September 10, 2026.
content.financial_impact: No universal refund or compensation applies to an entire product category; remedies depend on the specific product/seller/recall notice.
content.risk_if_ignored: MED-HIGH for a confirmed asbestos-containing product, especially if damaged or modified; the policy announcement itself is not evidence that an unlisted product is contaminated.
content.potential_benefit: Avoid unsafe listings and respond correctly if an owned product appears on an official asbestos or recall notice.
content.downside: Overreacting to category names can cause unnecessary disposal of products that have not been identified as containing asbestos.
content.what_would_change_mind: A new MHLW or Consumer Affairs Agency notice identifying additional specific products or changing handling instructions.

action_plan.goal: Check specific products against official notices without assuming an entire category is contaminated.
action_plan.who_should_act: Consumers who recently bought colored craft sand, diatomaceous-earth products or relevant safety/industrial products online, especially from unfamiliar marketplace sellers.
action_plan.deadline: No universal consumer deadline; act promptly if a specific owned product appears on an official asbestos or recall notice.
prepare: Official Consumer Affairs Agency and MHLW product-safety pages

steps.action: Record the brand, seller, product name/model and purchase listing.
steps.how: Use order history or packaging rather than relying on a generic category such as 'bath mat' or 'colored sand'.
steps.done_when: You can distinguish the exact item from similar products.

steps.action: Search the Consumer Affairs Agency recall information and MHLW asbestos-product list for the exact product or seller.
steps.how: Use government notices as the decision source, not social-media claims about the whole category.
steps.done_when: You know whether the product has been specifically identified by authorities.

steps.action: Use the handling/return/disposal instructions in the official notice or seller recall.
steps.how: Do not improvise destructive handling of a suspected asbestos product.
steps.done_when: You are following the official product-specific route.

mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming every colored-sand or diatomaceous product contains asbestos.
Breaking, grinding or sanding a suspected product to 'check' it yourself.
Relying on an online seller's reassurance when an official recall or asbestos notice says otherwise.

decision_rules.if: Your exact product appears on an official asbestos/recall notice
decision_rules.then: Follow that notice's handling and remedy instructions.

decision_rules.if: Only the generic product category matches but no official identification exists
decision_rules.then: Do not label the item contaminated; monitor official notices and verify the exact product.

action_plan.follow_up: Re-check the official product-safety pages if the marketplace listing disappears, the seller contacts you, or new government notices are issued.

outcomes: Understand what the Product Safety Pledge changes.
Know why a category-level warning is different from a product-specific asbestos finding.
learning.background: Japan's Product Safety Pledge is a voluntary government-industry framework with major online marketplaces aimed at reducing exposure to recalled or unsafe products. On September 10, asbestos-containing products and certain regulated equipment were added to its scope after authorities had identified prohibited products in online commerce.

terms.meaning: Products containing more than 0.1% asbestos by weight are prohibited from manufacture, import, transfer, provision and use under the cited Japanese law, subject to limited exceptions.
terms.why_it_matters: The rule is about measured asbestos content in a specific product, not the generic product category.

terms.meaning: A cooperative safety framework between Japanese authorities and online marketplace operators.
terms.why_it_matters: It helps marketplaces act on unsafe or recalled listings beyond ordinary consumer browsing.

how_it_works.title: Authorities identify unsafe product types or specific products
how_it_works.explanation: Government agencies publish safety findings and rules, including asbestos cases.

how_it_works.title: Marketplace operators use the pledge framework
how_it_works.explanation: Participating platforms cooperate to address listings that match unsafe or prohibited products.

learning.example: A diatomaceous bath mat is not automatically an asbestos product. The relevant question is whether the exact product has been identified in an official notice or otherwise verified above the legal threshold.
takeaways: The September 10 change expands online-marketplace safety coverage.
More than 0.1% asbestos by weight is prohibited under the cited law.
Past findings include colored sand and diatomaceous bath mats.
Do not generalize from one recalled product to an entire category.
Use official product-specific notices before acting.

30_sec: Japan expanded its online Product Safety Pledge on September 10 to include asbestos-containing products and certain regulated equipment.
Officials cited past unsafe colored sand and diatomaceous bath mats.
That does not mean all such products contain asbestos.
Check your exact product against official notices instead of relying on category rumors.
reading_levels.2_min: The Consumer Affairs Agency expanded Japan's Product Safety Pledge so online marketplaces can more systematically address asbestos-containing products and certain regulated equipment. The government cited past findings involving colored sand and diatomaceous bath mats. The legal issue is specific measured asbestos content above the threshold, not the mere fact that a product belongs to one of those categories. Consumers should identify the exact product and seller, check official CAA/MHLW notices, and follow product-specific instructions if a match is found.

editorial_visual.scene: an online shopping parcel and phone screen kept behind a protective inspection shield, with a tiny sealed sample icon and a government notice card, avoiding any dramatic dust imagery
editorial_visual.caption: Check the exact product, not the rumor
